subject: Delta Finance — Audit log exportability & retention questionnaire

Subject: Delta RFP — audit log export questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for agreeing to help with a few technical clarifications for our security questionnaire. Our compliance team has a short set of questions focused on audit logging, retention, and exportability that we need to include in the RFP. Can you confirm the following for Redwood?

- What events are included in the audit log (admin actions, API requests, model selection, configuration changes, etc.)?
- Default and maximum configurable retention windows for hosted vs. Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Export formats and programmatic export options (S3 sink, API, JSONL/CSV), and whether exports can include raw request/response payloads.
- Immutability and tamper-evidence capabilities; is there an append-only store or signed events?
- Time granularity and timezone handling for timestamps (UTC vs local).
- Any compliance certifications (SOC 2) or attestations related to logging features.

We attached our questionnaire as an Excel (Delta_Audit_Log_Questions.xlsx). If it's easier, a short written summary is fine — we'll use it in the RFP. Also, if there are constraints around hosted customers that differ from Dedicated/Private, please call those out.

Would appreciate a response by Monday so we can keep the RFP schedule.

Thanks,
Evan

Hi Evan —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can paste into the RFP. I've also attached a short audit-log spec and a draft copy of your questionnaire with inline answers (delta_questionnaire-draft.xlsx). If you want a cleaned PDF for the submission, say the word and well produce one.

Summary (high level):
- Events captured: Administrative actions (user and role changes, permission grants), platform configuration changes (model pinning, routing policy edits), API request metadata (request id, route, model version, prompt hashes, token counts), model outputs (optional — see raw payloads below), authentication events, error/exception traces, and system-level resource events (instance restarts, autoscale events).
- Retention: Hosted API default retention = 90 days for full request/response logs; retention can be extended to 1 year with paid retention add-on. Dedicated and Private deployments support configurable retention policies up to 7 years (customer-controlled). We can also implement shorter retention for specific routes on Dedicated/Private.
- Exportability: We support programmatic exports via:
  * S3-compatible sink (CSV, JSONL) for bulk exports;
  * Streaming export to customer-managed endpoints (SQS/Kinesis / custom HTTPS webhook) for near-real-time delivery;
  * Ad-hoc exports via API (paginated JSONL) for forensic pulls.
  * For Hosted customers, raw request/response payload inclusion in exports is optional but subject to data residency and PII controls; by default we redact prompt content unless the customer opts into storing raw payloads (consent + additional DPA terms required).
- Immutability & tamper evidence: Logs are written to append-only stores; for Dedicated/Private customers we can enable signed log chains (SHA-256 with KMS-managed keys) and provide log digests on request. For Hosted we maintain append-only retention internally and provide exportable digests for attestation.
- Timestamping: All logs use UTC timestamps with microsecond precision; we include an ISO-8601 timestamp and the customers configured timezone in the metadata.
- Compliance: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited; encryption at rest and in transit are standard (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit). We provide logging controls and evidence packages for audits (log sample extracts, retention policy configs, and access logs).

Operational notes / constraints:
- Large-scale exports (multi-GB to TB) are scheduled as background jobs; typical turnaround for a one-time export is 24-72 hours depending on volume. We offer managed export assistance for large customers (engineering-run export).
- Hosted customers cannot change underlying physical retention store but can purchase extended retention or export frequently to their own sinks.
- For PII-sensitive payloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments and use of customer-managed KMS for key isolation.

Next steps:
- If the RFP needs specific wording, we can produce a redlined section (we'll prepare a short PDF).
- If your compliance team wants a short call to walk the questionnaire, Marissa (sales lead) or Rishi (security lead) can join.

Best,

Soojin — thanks, this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before I populate the RFP: 

1) Per-route retention on Dedicated/Private: can customers set retention windows per API route (e.g., /inference/high-risk kept 365 days, /inference/low-risk kept 30 days)?
2) Raw payloads: You noted "optional" for hosted. For Dedicated: can the export include full unredacted request/response bodies, including prompt text and model output?
3) S3 sink: do you support signing to the customer's S3 (role-based write) or do you require credentials uploaded to Redwood? Also any constraints on bucket region?
4) For the signed log chain option, do you provide tooling to verify the chain locally or is it an attestation you provide?

If you could answer those 4 items inline thatd be great.

Thanks — Evan

Hi Evan — following up on Soojin's notes and answering your four points directly below: 

1) Per-route retention: Yes — on Dedicated and Private deployments customers can define retention policies at a route level. We expose a retention policy API and an admin console UI where you can map routes to retention windows. Hosted customers get per-API-key tagging and can request differing retention via support/paid add-on; per-route enforcement is available when you purchase the retention add-on or move to Dedicated.

2) Raw payloads: For Dedicated and Private, we can include unredacted request and response bodies in exports (including prompt text and model output) under the customer's data handling configuration. For Hosted, raw payload storage/export is opt-in and subject to DPA terms and regional data residency constraints.

3) S3 sink: We support role-based write via STS AssumeRole (recommended) and also accept short-lived credentials for upload. Buckets can be in any AWS region; for cross-region compliance we recommend keeping bucket and workload region aligned. We also support GCS and Azure Blob via equivalent role-based methods.

4) Signed log chain verification: We provide both — a verification CLI that can be run by customers to validate log digests against stored KMS signatures, and we can provide signed attestation artifacts for audit submissions. For Hosted customers we provide digest exports plus log export samples and a verification tool for digest checking; for Dedicated/Private we can arrange KMS key transfer or key-wrapping patterns as required.

If you'd like we can add these clarifications into the RFP language and send a one-page PDF. Also happy to schedule a 30-minute call with Soojin and Rishi to walk your compliance team through the answers.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
